newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki bourse extends losses as rate worries persist.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki bourse extends losses as rate worries persist.

text.p: Finnish shares fell for the fourth day running on Thursday and brokers took a gloomy view of the near-term future due to Wall Street weakness and continued interest rate woes.
The HEX all-share index closed 1.9 percent down at a six-week low 2,798.58 in moderate 620 million markka volume.
The FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark fell two percent to 975.38.
Telecoms company Nokia fell 7.20 markka to 301.00 markka.

Remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan -- seen signalling that U.S. interest rates may be in for a hike -- pointed to a new day of losses in the Finnish market on Friday, Helsinki brokers said.
This week's uncertainty about the timetable for European economic and monetary union continued and Finnish long-term interest rates rose further, adding to the jitters on the bourse.
Forest shares underperformed, falling 2.8 percent with UPM-Kymmene 3.90 markka lower at 104.10 markka. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
